title: Frontiers | The imbalance of self-reported wanting and liking is ...
abstract: The study investigated the association between the imbalance of self-reported wanting and liking and attentional bias towards smoking-related stimuli in smokers with low nicotine dependence. The findings indicated a positive correlation between higher levels of nicotine dependence and a greater discrepancy between wanting and liking. This imbalance was also positively correlated with better change detection performance for high salience smoking-related stimuli in smokers. The study supports the Incentive Sensitization Theory (IST) and suggests that attentional bias may develop early in nicotine addiction. It also implies that the underlying cognitive mechanisms might be partially accessible to conscious awareness, opening avenues for research and interventions.
